source: Find a Tender and Contracts Finder award notices in the Hub's digital lane (data/digital-lane.json), Open Government Licence v3.
sectionRule: Software and IT notices only. Each row is one supplier named on one Find a Tender or Contracts Finder award notice that an NHS buyer classified under a Common Procurement Vocabulary (CPV) code beginning 48 (software packages and information systems) or 72 (IT services). Those codes cover payroll, finance and office systems as much as clinical ones, so a row is not a claim of health technology. A row is counted as clinical only where the notice title names a clinical system. Medical device awards (CPV division 33) appear in the award sections above and are never repeated here.
laneRule: A Find a Tender or Contracts Finder notice is in this lane when the buyer name is an NHS body (contains "NHS", "Integrated Care Board" or "Health Board"; bare "Trust" is not a match) AND a Common Procurement Vocabulary (CPV) code on the notice begins 48 (software package and information systems) or 72 (IT services). An Atamis opportunity carries no CPV code, so its own Category text stands in: a software, information systems or IT services category, or a title naming a clinical digital system. Every Atamis authority is an NHS body by construction.
clinicalRule: CPV 48 and 72 are bought for payroll, finance, human resources and office systems as much as for clinical ones, so a lane row is not a claim of health technology. A row is flagged clinical only when its TITLE names a clinical system or a regulated digital product (electronic patient record, electronic prescribing, picture archiving and communication system (PACS), laboratory information management system (LIMS), artificial intelligence (AI), ambient voice, virtual ward, remote monitoring and the other terms in scripts/digital_lane_rules.py). Bare 'software', 'digital', 'IT' and 'licence' never flag a row. The speciality page shows clinical rows only.
matchRule: A supplier named on an award notice is attached to a Hub company only where the notice's name, normalised, is EXACTLY a normalised form of that company's own name or one of its recorded aliases. Normalisation lower-cases, turns & into and, drops punctuation, and strips trailing legal-form words (Ltd, Limited, plc, LLP, Inc, GmbH, BV, A/S, AB, Oy, Pty) and trailing territory words (UK, GB, England, Ireland, Europe, EMEA). Nothing else is stripped and there is no fuzzy, substring or edit-distance matching. A name matching two different companies, or none, is quarantined unpublished — it is a question for a human, never a best guess. One name is tried before that stripping: a notice name that a company holds verbatim, as its own name or a recorded alias, resolves to that company. This is narrower than the rule above, never wider, and it exists so two real companies whose names differ only by a territory word are told apart rather than quarantined against each other.

coverage.note: Only award notices the digital lane has read are here. Most NHS digital money moves as framework call-offs, which publish no notice of their own, so an empty section says what this index holds, not what a company has won.
